translations.text: He captured Arphaxad in the mountains of Ragau, pierced him with his spears, and destroyed him utterly that day.

In the eighteenth year, on the twenty-second day of the first month, a decision was made in the palace of Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Assyrians, to take revenge on the whole earth, just as he had said.

He told them to seize the mountain passes, because the road leading into Judea lay through them. It was easy to prevent anyone from passing through, since the approach was only wide enough for two men.

He said to them, “Tell me, people of Canaan, who are these people who live in the hill country? What cities do they inhabit? How large is their army? What is the basis of their power and strength? Who has risen over them as king and leads their army?”

Now that they have returned to their God, they have come back from the dispersion into which they were scattered. They have taken possession of Jerusalem, the place of their sanctuary, and settled in the hill country, because it was deserted.
“Lord, God of heaven, look down on their arrogance. Have mercy on the humiliation of our people, and look upon the faces of those who have humbled themselves before you today.”
The next day Holofernes ordered his entire army and all the people who had come with him to the war to march out for battle [?].
All the people gathered around Uzziah and the rulers of the city, along with their young men and their little children. They cried out and said before all the elders:
She sent her maid, who was in charge of her possessions, and summoned Chabris and Charmis, the elders of her city.
“But you must not attempt to force the plans of the Lord our God, because God is not like a human being who can be threatened, nor like a mortal who can be brought to judgment.”
When they saw her, with her appearance changed and her clothing different, they were utterly amazed at her beauty and said to her:

They did these things as they had said, and Judith went out with her maid. The men of the city watched her until she had descended the mountain and entered the valley, and they could no longer see her.
As she walked straight through the valley, the first Assyrian outpost met her.

“I have come to meet Holofernes, the commander-in-chief of your army, to tell him the truth and show him a road by which he can go and take control of the entire hill country, without a single one of his men uttering a cry or a breath of life.”
Judith said to him, “Listen to the words of your servant, and let your servant speak in your presence, for I will not lie to my lord tonight.”

“They have decided to consume the firstfruits of the grain and the tithes of the wine and oil, which they had kept and consecrated for the priests who stand before our God in Jerusalem—things that no one among the people is permitted even to touch with their hands.”
“There is no woman like her from one end of the earth to the other, in the beauty of her face and the wisdom of her words.”
The servants of Holofernes brought her to the tent. She slept until midnight, then rose during the morning watch.
When she came back in, she would remain purified in the tent until her food was brought to her in the evening.
Holofernes was delighted with her and drank an enormous amount of wine, more than he had ever drunk in a single day since the day he was born.
When she finished speaking, the people cheered loudly and raised a joyful shout in their city.
He went into the tent where Judith had been, but did not find her. He ran out to the people and cried out.
Trembling and fear fell upon them, and no one waited for the person beside him. Instead, they were thrown into confusion all at once and fled along every road across the plain and the hill country.
The rest of those living in Bethulia fell upon the Assyrian camp, plundered it, and became very wealthy.
Many desired her, but no man had sexual relations with her throughout her life after the day her husband Manasseh died and was gathered to his people.
